business_model: Subscription music streaming, no free ad-supported tier at launch

historical_evidence.company: Founded 2010 by Skype co-founders Janus Friis and Niklas Zennström, a subscription-based music-streaming service competing directly with Spotify in the same category and roughly the same launch window.
historical_evidence.market: Fast-growing, well-capitalized, intensely competitive music-streaming category as of 2012, with Spotify already the clear category leader by scale of funding and reported usage.
historical_evidence.team: Founded by proven, previously-successful entrepreneurs (Skype's founders) — a genuinely strong Founder-Market-Fit-adjacent signal, though building a proven track record in telecom/VoIP is a different domain than music/media licensing and consumer subscription products.
historical_evidence.product: Subscription-only streaming product (no free ad-supported tier), a structurally different go-to-market approach than Spotify's freemium model, requiring users to pay from day one rather than converting from a free tier.
historical_evidence.execution: Raised $50M in 2012 from institutional investors Fidelity and Morgan Stanley — a real, sophisticated-investor-backed capital raise, though smaller in scale than the funding rounds being closed by Spotify in the same period.
historical_evidence.traction: No specific subscriber-count figures were found in the contemporaneous sources reviewed for the snapshot date.
historical_evidence.financial: By comparison, Spotify was contemporaneously reported (mid-2012) to be raising at a $3B valuation off reported revenue of roughly $200M in the first six months of that year alone — a scale gap that was publicly visible and quantifiable at the time, not a retrospective judgment, and directly relevant to Rdio's Competitive Intensity read.

sources.title: Rdio Gets $108 Million in Equity Over 2 Years According to New Filings
How Spotify Turned Free Music into a $10+ Billion Valuation
sources.note: used only for the contemporaneous 2012 Spotify valuation/revenue figures cross-referenced against period reporting, not for Rdio-specific historical evidence

future_outcome.outcome_summary: Rdio was unable to close the funding and scale gap with Spotify and other well-capitalized competitors; the company filed for bankruptcy in November 2015, with Pandora acquiring its technology assets for $75 million.

benchmark_notes.why_included: Tests whether SIE's Competitive Intensity dimension correctly weighs a real, contemporaneously quantifiable funding/revenue scale gap against a direct, named competitor, rather than crediting Rdio's genuinely strong Founder-Market-Fit signal (proven Skype founders) as sufficient to offset it — a direct instance of the Differentiation-vs.-Defensibility-vs.-Competitive-Intensity distinction this methodology's design work has emphasized: Rdio's product may have been differentiated on UX grounds, but its Competitive Intensity position was genuinely weak given the scale gap.
benchmark_notes.known_ambiguities: The 2012 Spotify revenue/valuation figures were sourced from an aggregation site rather than a primary contemporaneous news article and are flagged Low confidence accordingly; the underlying comparison (Rdio meaningfully behind Spotify in scale as of 2012) is well-corroborated across multiple retrospective sources but the precise contemporaneous figures should be treated as directional, not exact.
benchmark_notes.evidence_limitations: No Rdio-specific subscriber count or revenue figures were located for the 2012 snapshot; this record leans heavily on the funding-round and competitive-landscape signals rather than direct company metrics.
